references.text: The Lord speaks to Moses about collecting gifts from the children of Israel for the sanctuary, which is the original command that Moses now conveys to the people.
Moses gathers the children of Israel and gives them all the commands that the Lord had spoken to him on Mount Sinai, a parallel situation where Moses delivers God's word to the congregation.
The Lord calls to Moses and speaks to him from the tent of meeting, instructing him to speak to the children of Israel—the same pattern where God commands and Moses conveys it to the people.
The Lord speaks to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai at the tent of meeting and gives commands that are to be conveyed to the congregation of Israel.
Moses speaks to all Israel and conveys what the Lord had commanded him, the same structure as in Exodus 35:4.
Contains the same phrasing 'This is what the Lord has commanded' (זֶה הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהוָה), a characteristic introduction to divine commands.
Moses says to the congregation, 'This is what the Lord has commanded should be done,' the same phrasing that introduces God's commands to the people.
Contains the phrase 'This is what the Lord has commanded,' showing the repeated pattern where Moses conveys God's specific commands.
Direct narrative connection: 35:4 gives the command, while 39:42 confirms it was carried out exactly as instructed.
